ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To burn incense is a literal action whose purpose changes with the surrounding ceremony.
EvidenceBody: The Collection for Resolving Chan Doubts narrates incense burned before a sacred image while establishing an oath. Huayan Shengke directly tells an unnamed monastic interlocutor to go light incense; Daxiu Zhu’s biography records incense burned before a prayer to celestial protectors and the buddhas; and the record of Fushi Qiyuan describes distant and nearby mourners burning incense and weeping at his death. Oath, instruction, prayer, and mourning are distinct settings for the same incense-burning action; none of these witnesses says that incense is burned into the body.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The exact witness joins incense before an image with the public establishment of an oath.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: No stored witness supports bodily incense burning; only one independent work remains, so the sense is provisional.
